data.title: Geely Rolls Out 2.25 MW EV Chargers in China with sub-Nine-Minute Charging
data.description:
Geely has started rolling out its new Smart Charging C12 stations in China, bringing a peak charging output of 2.25 MW (2,250 kW) per connector to several major cities.

According to Chinese media reports, the new chargers are already installed in Hangzhou, Shanghai, Ningbo, Jiaxing and Xi’an. Geely unveiled the fifth-generation charging system in Ningbo on September 23.

While the 2,250 kW is impressive, it is the charger’s peak output rather than what current vehicles can accept. CarNewsChina reports that the compatible Zeekr 001 and Lynk & Co 10 currently top out at around 1,100 kW.

Still, paired with Geely’s new 12C Shendun Golden Battery, the charging times are extremely quick. In Geely’s tests, the two models charged from 10 to 70 per cent in 4 minutes and 30 seconds, and from 10 to 97 per cent in just 8 minutes and 40 seconds.

Geely says its Xingrui PowerMind AI system predicts battery temperature up to 30 seconds in advance and adjusts charging power, while an end-to-end liquid cooling system helps manage temperatures throughout the charging process.

The rollout adds another player to China’s rapidly growing megawatt charging race. BYD’s megawatt Flash Charging system peaks at 1,500 kW per connector, with the automaker having already deployed more than 10,000 Flash Charging stations across China, with a goal to reach 20,000 by year-end.

Geely hasn’t announced any Canadian charging plans for the technology, though it has been hiring in Toronto as it prepares for a Canadian launch. The company has also recently expanded its charging interests through a battery-swapping deal with NIO Power.

data.title: Rivian Beats Wall Street Estimates With Record Q3 2026 Deliveries
data.description:
Rivian set a new quarterly delivery record in Q3 2026, beating Wall Street expectations as the EV maker continues to ramp production of the new R2.

The company announced on Friday that it delivered 19,248 vehicles during the three months ending September 30, comfortably ahead of the roughly 18,000 deliveries analysts were expecting.

Deliveries were also up sharply from earlier this year. Rivian handed over 12,194 vehicles in Q2, meaning deliveries jumped 57.8% quarter-over-quarter. Compared with the 13,201 vehicles delivered in Q3 2025, the latest figure represents a 45.8% increase.

Production followed a similar trajectory. Rivian built 19,751 vehicles during the quarter, up from 12,613 in Q2. All of those vehicles were produced at the company’s lone manufacturing facility in Normal, Illinois.

The 19,248 deliveries also set a new quarterly record for Rivian. The previous high was 15,564 vehicles in Q3 2023.

The major reason for the boost in both production and deliveries is the arrival of the R2. Customer deliveries of Rivian’s smaller and less expensive SUV began in June, making Q3 the first full quarter with R2 deliveries included in the totals.

Rivian does not provide a model-by-model breakdown, so it is unclear how many of the quarter’s deliveries were R2s. The company is currently selling only the higher-priced R2 Performance through the end of 2026 as it ramps production.

That ramp is still evolving. Rivian previously said it expected to scale R2 production to two shifts by the end of Q3, although the company had not announced the start of that second shift as of Friday morning. Rivian has also pushed customer availability of the R2’s LiDAR hardware to 2027.

Rivian reaffirmed its full-year guidance of 65,000 to 70,000 deliveries, a range it raised in July from 62,000 to 67,000. Rivian said its Q3 production and delivery results were in line with its outlook.

With 41,807 vehicles delivered through the first nine months, Rivian needs at least 23,193 deliveries in Q4 to reach the bottom of its guidance, or 28,193 to reach the top

Rivian will report its full Q3 financial results on Thursday, October 29, after the market closes.

data.title: Get Paid To Charge at Home: Compare EV Charging Rewards Program in Canada
data.description:
EV charging rewards programs are becoming more common in Canada, giving drivers more ways to earn money from charging at home. But with new operators entering the market all the time, knowing which is the best program beyond simply the advertised rate can be difficult.

To help, we’ve launched a new EV charging rewards page that brings 20 programs together in one place.

The page compares programs that share Clean Fuel Regulations credit revenue with drivers. Each listing explains who runs the program, which hardware it supports, how and when you get paid, and how to sign up.

For Tesla owners, a dedicated filter makes it easier to find compatible options. WattsApp, RoadToEV and Roulez Électrique Club accept the Tesla Wall Connector, while most other programs require an OCPP-compatible charger. You can also filter the listings by province and charger type.

A built-in earnings estimator helps you compare potential annual payouts. It defaults to 3,500 kWh of home charging per year, but you can adjust that figure using a slider or enter your own usage. Estimates use each program’s highest advertised rate, so your actual earnings may be lower.

Before enrolling, there are a few details to check beyond the advertised rate. Many programs pay only once a year, and their payout schedules and exit terms vary.

One of the most important rules to understand before switching providers is that a charger can only be enrolled in one program per calendar year. If you’re already enrolled, signing up with another provider in the same year could disqualify your charger from both programs, leaving you without a payout.

If you plan to switch, you need to leave your current program before December 31 and join the new one on or after January 1. Check the operator’s exit terms in advance so you know what is required.

Visit our EV charging rewards page to compare the programs available where you live and see how much your home charging could earn.

data.title: Cadillac Optiq EV Recalled for Power Window Safety Issue
data.description:
General Motors (GM) is recalling nearly 30,000 Cadillac Optiq electric SUVs in the U.S. over a software issue that could prevent the front windows from detecting an obstruction when being closed remotely.

According to a filing with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), the recall covers 29,347 Optiqs from the 2025, 2026 and 2027 model years. Affected vehicles were built between July 24, 2024 and September 22, 2026.

Transport Canada has not yet issued a similar recall.

The issue is limited to a specific situation involving the key fob’s express-up function. When the front windows are remotely closed, they may fail to stop and reverse if an obstruction is encountered during the final 13 mm (0.5 inches) of travel.

That creates the possibility of a passenger being pinched by the closing glass.

“When the express-up feature on the front power windows is activated using the key fob, the windows may fail to stop and reverse automatically if they encounter an object during the final 13 mm of upward travel,” GM said in its filing.

According to GM, the issue was traced to a software calibration from supplier Kwangjin America. The upper travel range for the anti-pinch system had been set too low, preventing the system from consistently meeting the required stop-and-reverse performance.

The problem was first brought to GM’s attention in June after a dealer noticed the windows on four 2026 Optiqs were not reversing properly. GM later tested five vehicles, with four failing to consistently stop and reverse under certain conditions.

GM corrected the calibration in production on September 22.

Fortunately for owners, the recall won’t require any new hardware. GM will update the body control module (BCM) software free of charge. Some Optiqs can receive the fix through an over-the-air (OTA) update, while other owners can have the software installed at a dealership.

You can read the full NHTSA recall notice below.

data.title: Tesla cuts AI5 memory for Optimus, but not as much as originally planned
data.description:
Tesla is cutting the amount of memory in its next-generation AI5 and AI6 chips to lower costs and help scale Optimus production, although Elon Musk has already walked back part of the reduction.

In a post on X on Thursday, Musk initially announced that Tesla was cutting AI5 memory in half, from 144GB to 72GB of LPDDR5 (LP5). AI6 is also being reduced by one-third, which works out to a drop from 216GB to 144GB of LP6.

LP5 and LP6 deliver high memory bandwidth while consuming less power than conventional desktop/server memory.

However, just hours later Musk said Tesla had decided 72GB was a little too low. The company is still cutting AI5’s memory significantly, but will now settle on 96GB instead.

There was no corresponding change announced for AI6, which remains at 144GB.

Despite reducing the amount of memory, Musk believes the impact on Optimus will be minimal because memory bandwidth is more important to its performance than total capacity.

The decision comes as the AI industry continues to put pressure on memory supplies. Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra said this week that humanoid robots could eventually require more than 200GB of memory and several terabytes (TB) of storage per unit, although his comments were about the industry generally and did not specifically reference Tesla.

The changes come as AI5 has reportedly entered trial production. Samsung has completed its version of the chip and is preparing to manufacture it using its 2nm process at its Taylor, Texas, facility, but volume production is not expected until 2027.

But don’t put off buying a Tesla hoping it will have AI5. Tesla plans to prioritize AI5 for Optimus and AI training before eventually introducing the chip into its vehicles.

data.title: Geely launches Canadian website ahead of launch
data.description:
Geely has become the latest Chinese automaker to establish a Canadian web presence, launching a dedicated website as it prepares to bring its vehicles to Canada.

According to Geely’s Canadian website, geely.ca, they have plans to establish a dealer network as part of its expansion into the country. “Our Canadian journey is coming soon, with a growing dealer network planned for key markets across the country.” The site does not identify any cities, dealership groups or planned locations.

There are also plenty of details still missing. The site lists no vehicles, pricing, specifications, reservations or launch date, referring only to a “new generation of electrified vehicles.” Geely’s corporate profile lists Geely Auto, Lynk & Co and Zeekr as group brands, but gives no indication that the latter two are part of its Canadian plans.

Interestingly, the French-language version provides a little more detail, saying Geely’s Canadian journey is expected to begin in the first quarter of 2027 with a dealer network expanding across major markets. The English page has no corresponding date.

The website is the latest sign Geely has been preparing to launch EV sales in Canada. In April, we reported on the company hiring in Toronto for six senior positions tied to the “Geely Auto Brand.” A month later, EX5 and EX2 test vehicles were spotted arriving at Toronto Pearson, although Geely has not announced Canadian launch plans for either vehicle.

Geely isn’t the first Chinese automaker to establish a Canadian website ahead of its market entry. In August, BYD launched its Canadian website, which continues to display a “COMING SOON” message but does not provide a launch date, Canadian vehicle lineup or pricing. Like Geely, BYD has also been laying the groundwork behind the scenes, including hiring for Canadian operations and dealer development.

More recently, Chery Group’s Omoda and Jaecoo brands launched their own Canadian website. Their plans are a little more specific, with the site saying the two brands are “coming late 2026” and that a dealer network is being built across Canada. However, like BYD and Geely, Omoda and Jaecoo have yet to reveal Canadian pricing or a confirmed vehicle lineup.

Geely and other Chinese automakers are entering the Canadian market after Ottawa introduced a 49,000-vehicle quota for Chinese EV imports at a 6.1% tariff, effective March 1. Geely-owned Lotus has already sent its first Lotus Eletre shipment to Canada under the new framework in May, but so far Tesla has taken the majority of the quota in the first window.

data.title: Canadian Astronaut Joshua Kutryk Reaches ISS as SpaceX Crew-13 Sets Docking Record
data.description:
Canadian astronaut Joshua Kutryk has arrived at the International Space Station (ISS), completing his first trip to space while helping SpaceX set a new U.S. launch-to-docking record. Kutryk and his three Crew-13 crewmates docked aboard Dragon Grace at the forward port of the station’s Harmony module at 7:05 p.m. ET Thursday, according to NASA.

The docking came just 7 hours and 55 minutes after launch, making it the fastest trip from launch to the ISS by a U.S. spacecraft in the station’s history.

Crew-13 lifted off at 11:10 a.m. ET from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station. Joining Kutryk are NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, along with Roscosmos cosmonaut Sergey Teteryatnikov.

After docking, the crew remained aboard Dragon for just over two hours before the hatch opened at 9:19 p.m. ET, allowing them to enter their new home for the next several months.

For Kutryk, the flight marks several milestones. The Alberta-born Royal Canadian Air Force colonel is the first Canadian Space Agency astronaut to fly under NASA’s Commercial Crew Program. His mission is also Canada’s fourth long-duration stay aboard the ISS.

During his approximately six months in orbit, Kutryk will participate in Canadian and international research, with much of his work focused on human health. Experiments will study areas including bone density, cardiorespiratory health, anemia, mental health and how astronauts perceive orientation in microgravity.

The mission comes just six months after fellow Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen travelled around the Moon aboard Artemis II.

Crew-13 is SpaceX’s 13th operational crew rotation mission for NASA and its 14th crewed flight to the ISS under the Commercial Crew Program when including Demo-2.

The crew also continued a tradition dating back to 2020 by riding to the launch pad in Teslas. For Crew-13, the cars were fittingly equipped with “Lucky 13” plates.

data.title: Tesla beats expectations with 486,532 deliveries in Q3 2026
data.description:
Tesla has reported its Q3 2026 production and delivery results, beating expectations as deliveries increased from the previous quarter. Energy storage deployments also increased, but came in slightly lower than expectations.

According to figures released on Friday, Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles globally in Q3 2026, above the 461,974 deliveries analysts had expected according to Tesla’s own company-compiled consensus. The result was a beat of 24,558 vehicles, or 5%.

Deliveries increased by 6,406 vehicles, or 1%, from the 480,126 vehicles delivered in Q2 2026. However, they were down 2% from the 497,099 in Q3 2025, which itself was an all-time quarterly record.

Unsurprisingly, Model 3/Y accounted for 478,237 deliveries, while Tesla reported 8,295 deliveries under “Other Models.” That category includes Model S, Model X, Cybertruck and Semi, although Tesla does not provide a breakdown between those vehicles. Tesla does not report Canadian deliveries separately.

Production reached 464,391 vehicles, consisting of 457,387 Model 3/Y vehicles and 7,004 other models. Deliveries exceeded production by 22,141 vehicles during the quarter, implying Tesla drew down inventory by about 22,000 vehicles.

Deliveries beat consensus but trail previous quarter

The 486,532 deliveries represented a 1% increase from Q2 2026 but a 2% decline compared with Q3 2025. Model 3/Y deliveries increased 2% quarter over quarter to 478,237 but were 1% lower year over year.

Other-model deliveries moved in the opposite direction, falling 33% from 12,364 in Q2 2026 and 48% from 15,933 a year earlier. This is likely due to the discontinuation of Model S/S, which surprisingly didn’t have a large impact on production – total production increased 3% from Q2 2026 and 4% from Q3 2025.

Energy storage misses expectations

Tesla deployed 13.7 GWh of energy storage products during Q3 2026, 2.2 GWh, or 14%, below the company-compiled consensus of 15.9 GWh.

Deployments were up 0.2 GWh, or 1%, from 13.5 GWh in Q2 2026 and increased 1.2 GWh, or 10%, from 12.5 GWh in Q3 2025. The quarterly total was also 0.5 GWh, or 4%, below the all-time quarterly storage record of 14.2 GWh set in Q4 2025.

Earnings date

Tesla will post its financial results for the third quarter of 2026 after market close on Wednesday, October 21, 2026. Tesla management will hold their live Q&A session that day at 4:30 p.m. CT (5:30 p.m. ET).

data.title: Tesla rolls out Model 3 upgrades in the U.S., but Canada still left out
data.description:
Tesla is bringing another round of upgrades to the Model 3, this time for the U.S., Puerto Rico and Mexico.

The changes were announced by Tesla Thursday evening, just one day after we reported on similar changes in China and other Asia-Pacific markets, but one feature is notable absent.

According to a post from Tesla North America on X, every trim of the new Model 3 now gets the larger 16-inch HD center touchscreen, replacing the previous 15.4-inch display.

The larger display is the same size as the one introduced on the Model Y earlier this year and rolled out to Model 3 in China this week. The upgrade was also first spotted in Tesla’s backend code in February.

There are some performance improvements as well. The Model 3 Premium AWD can now accelerate from 0-60 mph in 3.8 seconds, a substantial improvement from the previous 4.2 seconds.

Its range remains unchanged at 346 miles (about 557 km).

The Model 3 Performance also gets a black headliner and a modest range boost, climbing 2.3% from 309 miles (497 km) to 316 miles (509 km). Peak power has also increased to 528 hp, compared with the 510 hp Tesla listed when the updated Performance launched in 2024. Its 2.9-second 0-60 mph time remains unchanged.

Tesla hasn’t explained what hardware changes are behind the additional power and range, or whether any of the improvements can make their way to previously delivered vehicles. U.S. Pricing is also unchanged.

Despite all these changes, Vehicle-to-Load (V2L) is still missing. The feature was announced for Model 3 and expanded to all Model Y tricks in China and other markets the night before, so its absence is a bit strange.

Another thing that isn’t changing is the white interior, at least for now. U.S. buyers can still select black and white, while the new Zen Grey option introduced overseas hasn’t appeared in the U.S. configurator.

Tesla hasn’t announced these changes for Canada. The company’s announcement names only the U.S., Puerto Rico and Mexico. Canada’s Model 3 comes from Giga Shanghai, but Tesla hasn’t said when these updates will reach Canadian orders.

data.title: Tesla addresses safety concerns with Supercharger ‘Emergency Drive Away’
data.description:
Tesla is introducing a new feature that lets drivers leave a Supercharger without first getting out to unplug, giving owners a way to escape a dangerous situation while charging.

Called Emergency Drive Away, the feature allows a vehicle to shift into Drive with the charging cable still connected. It is rolling out free through software update 2026.38.3, although Tesla says it currently applies only to U.S. Superchargers. Model S and Model X vehicles built before 2021 are also excluded.

How to use Emergency Drive Away

Using it is straightforward. Simply plug in like you normally would. If find yourself in a situation where you need to drive away quickly, shift into Drive, and an “Emergency Drive Away” message will appear on the main display. Hold the brake pedal and tap ‘Activate’ to enable the feature – then drive away.

There is a significant tradeoff however as using it will damage both the vehicle and charging equipment. As a result, Tesla warns that deliberate misuse will bring additional penalties, and that using the feature will automatically send a recording of the event to Tesla.

You can watch the video from Tesla demonstrating the feature below.

Why did Tesla add this?

The new feature comes following renewed concerns about being unable to flee while charging after an August 1 shooting in Twin Falls, Idaho. The attack near an In-N-Out restaurant and adjacent Supercharger left three people dead and several injured, including a driver shot while sitting in a charging Tesla.

The incident prompted owners to call for an emergency escape function, and Tesla has responded.

Until now, aftermarket company EVject has offered one way around that problem. Its Escape Connector sits between the charging cable and vehicle, allowing drivers to disconnect without stepping outside. The adapter permanently separates during an emergency departure, which the company says helps protect the car and charger.

EVject’s approach has also faced scrutiny. As previously reported by Drive Tesla, Tesla sued the company in 2024 over alleged overheating risks, and EVject subsequently agreed to recall its original connectors. Its current design includes thermal protection.

Tesla’s update brings an escape option without requiring an accessory. For Canadian owners, however, availability remains an unanswered question as Tesla has not announced when Emergency Drive Away might expand beyond U.S. Superchargers.
